msItem.title: Psalterium cum canticis, credo, litaniis sanctorum etc.

provenance.orgName: Whitby, Yorkshire, Benedictine abbey of St Peter and St Hilda
provenance.p: Listed as an untraced book under Whitby in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964), and again in the Supplement (1987). The manuscript was untraced when the corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card was originally written. As such, the index card could only relay provenance evidence as reported in previous sales catalogues (see details of sales below). Specifically, the index card noted an inscription in a later hand, Abbatia de Whitby in com. Ebor, and the presence of Hilda and other saints in the litany. However, since the fragmentary Psalter reappeared in 2006, the Whitby attribution has been refuted. See Peter Kidd, The "Whitby" Psalter, mssprovenance blog, post dated 26 March 2022. Kidd cites Nigel Morgan, English Monastic Litanies of the Saints after 1100 (London, 2013), pp. 28-29: The litany on ff. 25r-28r on examination has turned out to be a secular text of the use of York and in no way connected with Whitby. In light of the aforementioned research, the Whitby attribution was changed from accepted to rejected during Medieval Libraries of Great Britain data reconciliation work in 2026.

history.provenance: Sold from library unstated at Sotheby's 14 December 1911 (lot 394).
J. J. Leighton, Catalogue of Manuscripts (1912), no. 259.

Sotheby 8 March 1937 lot 1172 (Lt. Col. W. E. Moss sale) to Dulau for £25. This was the location reported in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964). Compare a note on the index card in Ker's hand: Wrote [i.e. to Dulau] 15.7.40, but whereabouts not known by D. The following update was provided in the Medieval Libraries of Great Britain Supplement (1987): Lt.-Col. Moss's psalter has been split up. One bifolium is owned by Prof. T Takamiya, Tokyo, and four leaves by Mr S. J. Keynes, London.

33 leaves purchased by Harvard University in 2006 (further acquisition details in Hollis catalogue entry). For other known fragments, see Peter Kidd, Notes and Observations, mssprovenance blog (no date).
